title: Prime-to-p torsors on a strict-local boundary puncture split at a finite root level
statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Assume $R$ is strictly henselian, meaning henselian with separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, $r\geq0$, be distinct members of a regular system of parameters of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Put $f=t_1\cdots t_r$ (empty product $1$) and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[1/f]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $G$ be a finite group with $p\nmid |G|$, and let $P\to U$ be a finite etale surjection [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] with an action of the constant group $G$ over $U$ which is simply transitive on every geometric fibre; equivalently it is a $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. No connectedness of $P$ is assumed.

There is an integer $n\geq1$ with $(n,p)=1$ such that, on putting
$$R_n=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),\qquad U_n=\operatorname{Spec}R_n[1/f],$$
using multivariate polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], the base change $P\times_U U_n$ is isomorphic over $U_n$ to the trivial torsor $\coprod_{g\in G}U_n$, with its regular $G$-action. The map $U_n\to U$ is induced by the displayed $R$-algebra structure. In particular, $r=0$ asserts that every such torsor over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is trivial, with $n=1$.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1(i) and its strict-local parameter-root normal form, printed pp.133-134. Agent-formulated prime-to-p-group consequence: such torsors are tame, and the normal form is dominated by one finite simultaneous root cover. This is not a statement that a cover of prime-to-p degree without a prime-to-p Galois group is tame.

proof.text: Put $n=|G|$. Since a group contains its identity, $n\geq1$. The hypothesis $p\nmid |G|$ and primality of $p$ give integers $a,b$ with $an+bp=1$. In the characteristic-$p$ ring $R$ this reads $(a\cdot1_R)(n\cdot1_R)=1$, so $n$ is a unit in $R$, and $(n,p)=1$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 and paragraph 2.2, printed pp.133-134: invertible-order specialization; elementary Bezout calculation.

proof.text: Write $B=R_n$ and extend the specified parameter list to $t_1,\ldots,t_d$, where $d=\dim R$. Successive applications of [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] to $T^n-t_i$ give the unique expansion $\sum_a c_a x^a$ in $B$, with $0\leq a_i<n$. The successive one-variable presentations equal the displayed multivariate quotient: both classify tuples satisfying the same equations. Thus $B$ is finite free over $R$, and its coefficient of $1$ proves injectivity of $R\to B$. It is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Tags 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian, monic quotient calculation), 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$. The closed fibre is $B/\mathfrak mB=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n,\ldots,x_r^n)$. Each prime contains all $x_i$, and the quotient by those elements is $k$, so this nonzero fibre is local with residue field $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product], $B$ is a finite product of nonzero henselian local $R$-algebras, with local structural maps. Each factor has nonzero reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$. There is exactly one factor, since otherwise the local closed fibre would have a nontrivial idempotent; in a local ring an idempotent $e$ has either $e$ or $1-e$ invertible and is $1$ or $0$. Thus $B$ is henselian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB+(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ and residue field $k$. The latter is separably closed, so $B$ is strictly henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

source.place: Tags 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian) and 04GF (definition-henselian); explicit closed-fibre calculation.

proof.text: The maximal ideal just obtained is $(x_1,\ldots,x_r,t_{r+1},\ldots,t_d)$, since $t_i=x_i^n$ for $i\leq r$. Its $d$ generators give $\dim B\leq d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators]. For every chain of primes of $R$, [pqf-lem-lying-over] lifts its first prime through the injective integral map $R\to B$, and repeated [pqf-lem-going-up] lifts the remaining chain. The lifted inclusions are strict because their contractions are distinct. Hence $\dim B\geq\dim R=d$. Thus $B$ is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme], and its displayed generators are a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], both $R$ and $B$ are domains. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, with the inclusion induced by $R\hookrightarrow B$.

source.place: Tags 00KQ (proposition-dimension), 00GQ (lemma-integral-overring-surjective), 00GU (lemma-integral-going-up), 00KU (definition-regular-local), 00NP (lemma-regular-domain).

proof.text:
For each $i\leq r$, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], allowing a permutation of the generators, makes both $R/(t_i)$ and $B/(x_i)$ regular local. They are domains by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], and $t_i,x_i$ are nonzerodivisors. Their quotient presentations give
$$B/(x_i)=(R/(t_i))[x_j:j\ne i]/(x_j^n-\bar t_j:j\ne i).$$
Repeated [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] makes this finite free over $R/(t_i)$ with a basis containing $1$, so that map is injective. Consequently $\mathfrak p_i=(t_i)$ and $\mathfrak q_i=(x_i)$ are prime and $\mathfrak q_i\cap R=\mathfrak p_i$. The displayed quotient identification follows by imposing $x_i=0$, which also imposes $t_i=0$, and leaves exactly the other root equations.

source.place: Tags 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), 00NP (lemma-regular-domain), and 04GG (monic quotient calculation).

proof.text: Set $V_i=R_{\mathfrak p_i}$ and $A_i=B_{\mathfrak q_i}$. By [lem-sbc-regular-principal-prime-localization-dvr] these are DVRs, with uniformizers $t_i,x_i$. In fact $B\otimes_R V_i=A_i$. To see this, $B\otimes_R V_i$ is finite over $V_i$, hence integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Every maximal ideal contracts to the maximal ideal of $V_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal] and contains $x_i$ because $x_i^n=t_i$. Its quotient by $x_i$ is the generic fibre of the finite free domain $B/(x_i)$ over $R/(t_i)$. That fibre is a nonzero finite-dimensional domain over a field, hence a field: multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective and therefore surjective linear endomorphism. There is therefore exactly one maximal ideal, and localization at it is already this ring, proving the equality with $A_i$. The map $V_i\to A_i$ is finite and injective, has fraction fields $K\to E$, and satisfies $\mathfrak m_{V_i}A_i=(t_i)=(x_i^n)=\mathfrak m_{A_i}^n$. Since $A_i$ is a DVR, $\mathfrak q_i$ has height one (prime chains correspond under localization). Every height-one prime of $B$ containing $f=\prod_i x_i^n$ contains some $x_i$ and hence equals $\mathfrak q_i$.

source.place: Tags 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 00OI (lemma-going-up-maximal-on-top); explicit localization and closed-fibre calculation.

proof.text: Let $U_B=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$, with exactly the $R$-algebra map in the statement, and put $P_B=P\times_U U_B$. By [lem-sbc-galois-cover-base-change] it is a finite etale $G$-torsor, including its action and simple transitivity. Apply [lem-sbc-field-torsor-galois-components] first to $P_K$, obtaining its generic algebra $\prod_j L_j$, with $L_j/K$ finite Galois and $[L_j:K]\mid n$. Apply it also to $(P_B)_E$, obtaining a finite product $D=\prod_a F_a$ of finite Galois, in particular separable, extensions of $E$. These are the actual generic algebras over their given structure maps. The fibre product gives $D=(\prod_j L_j)\otimes_K E=\prod_j(L_j\otimes_K E)$; each field factor $F_a$ comes from one $j$, since the orthogonal idempotents of a finite product map to $0$ or $1$ in a field. The torsor is nonempty, so $D\ne0$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), pp.133-134, simultaneous-root Abhyankar argument expanded using the finite etale field-torsor decomposition (Stacks Tags 03SF, 03QR).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal], $B$ is a normal Noetherian domain. For each $a$ let $C_a$ be its integral closure in $F_a$. The finite-separable integral-closure theorem [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] makes $C_a$ finite over $B$. Put $C=\prod_a C_a$, a finite $B$-algebra embedded in $D$. This finiteness uses separability over $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, already supplied in step 7, and does not require excellence. Localizations of $B[1/f]$ are localizations of $B$, so the same regularity and normality statements also make $B[1/f]$ normal.

source.place: Tags 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular), 0567 (lemma-regular-normal), 032L (lemma-Noetherian-normal-domain-finite-separable-extension).

proof.text: Write $T$ for the finite $B[1/f]$-algebra of the affine scheme $P_B$, using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. By [lem-sbc-finite-etale-open-generic-algebra], applied with $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and open $U_B$, $T$ embeds in an $E$-algebra. Hence nonzero base elements act injectively on $T$, and its canonical generic map $T\to T\otimes_{B[1/f]}E=D$ is injective. This $D$ is the total quotient ring of $T$: if a nonzerodivisor $z\in T$ had a zero coordinate in $D$, the nonzero idempotent on that coordinate would be $t/b$ for some $t\in T$ and nonzero base denominator $b$. Then $t\ne0$ but $zt=0$, a contradiction. Thus all nonzerodivisors of $T$ are units of $D$; conversely every element of $D$ is already a fraction with a nonzerodivisor base denominator. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal], $T$ is normal. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total] makes it integrally closed in this very $D$.

source.place: Tags 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up), 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed); finite etale generic injection as in Stacks Tags 02GL and 081I.

proof.text: The finite-algebra theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes $T$ integral over $B[1/f]$. An element of $D$ integral over $B[1/f]$ is also integral over $T$, by its same monic equation, and hence lies in $T$ by step 9. Thus $T$ is exactly the integral closure of $B[1/f]$ in $D$. Integral closure in a finite product is the product of the integral closures: project a monic equation for one direction; for the other, multiply finitely many monic equations, one annihilating each coordinate. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] to each $C_a\subset F_a$. It identifies $C[1/f]$ with $T$ as subalgebras of $D$, respecting their structural maps. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}C$ restricts over $U_B$ to the actual $P_B$.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); explicit normalization identification.

proof.text: For each $i,j$, apply [lem-sbc-dvr-galois-normalization-ramification-dvd] to the DVR $V_i$, its fraction field $K$, and $L_j/K$. Step 7 gives the required Galois hypothesis and $[L_j:K]\mid n$. At every prime above the maximal ideal of $V_i$, both the ramification index and the residue degree of its integral closure in $L_j$ divide $n$. Step 1 makes $n$ a unit in $V_i$. These are precisely the two divisibility assumptions in the DVR tame tensor-factor theorem; no assertion about a multi-divisor cover has been taken from a single-divisor splitting theorem.

source.place: Tag 09EB (lemma-galois-conclusion), degree formula, applied separately at each parameter divisor.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and a factor $F_a$ coming from $L_j$. Since $t_i$ is invertible in $L_j$ and $A_i[1/t_i]=E$, one has $L_j\otimes_{V_i}A_i=L_j\otimes_K E$. Thus $F_a$ is a maximal field quotient of the tensor algebra in [lem-sbc-dvr-tame-tensor-factor-unramified], with its specified right-hand $A_i$-structure. The integral closure $S_a$ of $A_i$ in $F_a$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite], since $F_a/E$ is finite separable. Step 6 gives the finite faithful map $V_i\to A_i$ and root index $n$; step 11 gives both divisibilities, and $n>0$ is a unit. The cited DVR tensor-factor theorem therefore gives $\Omega_{(S_a)_Q/A_i}=0$ at every prime above $\mathfrak m_{A_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], $S_a=C_a\otimes_B A_i$. Localizing once more identifies these local rings with $(C_a)_{\mathfrak Q}$ for $\mathfrak Q$ above $\mathfrak q_i$. Hence $\Omega_{(C_a)_{\mathfrak Q}/B_{\mathfrak q_i}}=0$ for all such $\mathfrak Q$.

source.place: Tag 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), as formulated in the live DVR tensor-factor theorem; Tag 0307 (integral-closure localization).

proof.text: The finite $B$-algebra $C$ is of finite type: its module generators also generate it as an algebra. As $B$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes it finitely presented. For a prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak q_i$, its localization is the localization of one $C_a\subset F_a$ (the product idempotents select exactly one factor). This local ring is torsion-free over the DVR $A_i=B_{\mathfrak q_i}$, since it embeds in $F_a$. A DVR is a PID by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] gives flatness of this local ring over $A_i$. Its differentials over $A_i$ vanish by step 12. The base-change isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], followed by target localization [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], identifies this module with $(\Omega_{C/B})_{\mathfrak Q}$. The equivalence (3)$\Rightarrow$(2) in [lem-sc-etale-at-prime-flat-unramified-criterion] now gives a basic neighbourhood $D(g)$ of $\mathfrak Q$ in $\operatorname{Spec}C$ whose map to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale. Thus all points over every height-one boundary prime have such a neighbourhood.

source.place: Tags 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation), 00PD (DVR criterion), 00U6 and 08WD (pointwise etale criterion); More on Algebra Tag 0AUW (torsion-free over a PID).

proof.text: Let $N=\operatorname{Spec}C$. Its restriction over $U_B$ is etale by step 10. Composing with the open immersion $U_B\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$ remains etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Let $O\subset N$ be the union of that inverse image and all source-open neighbourhoods obtained in step 13. The restriction $O\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale, since this is checked on an open cover as in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The complement $Z=N\setminus O$ is closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] its image under the finite map $N\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is closed. Set $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\setminus\operatorname{image}(Z)$. Then $W$ is open, contains $U_B$ and every height-one point, and $N_W\to W$ is finite etale. Indeed the inverse image of $W$ lies in $O$ and is a restriction of this finite map. The generic point belongs to $U_B$, since $B$ is a domain and $f\ne0$.

source.place: Tags 02GP (open immersions etale), 02GN (composition), 01WN (finite morphisms are proper and closed); open-cover locality in the definition of etaleness.

proof.text: Every point outside $W$ has height at least two, since $W$ contains the generic point and every height-one point. Its local ring is $B_{\mathfrak q}$, regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. The prime correspondence for localization identifies its dimension with the supremum of lengths of prime chains below $\mathfrak q$, so that dimension is at least two. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sbc-regular-codimension-two-etale-extension] to the open $W$ and the finite etale morphism $N_W\to W$. It supplies a finite etale morphism $H\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ and an isomorphism $H_W\cong N_W$ over $W$. Restricting to the specified open $U_B\subset W$ and using step 10 gives $H_{U_B}\cong P_B$ over $U_B$. This uses the general live extension theorem across a regular codimension-two boundary, not the dropped finite-normalization purity node.

source.place: Tags 0BMA (lemma-local-purity) and 0EY7 (lemma-extend-pure), regular codimension-two finite-etale extension.

proof.text: The finite map $H\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is surjective. Its closed image, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], contains the generic point: over that point it agrees with the nonempty torsor $(P_B)_E$. A closed subset of the spectrum of a domain containing its generic point is the whole spectrum. The ring $B$ is strictly henselian by step 3. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-strict-henselian-algebra-etale-section] with $H=A=B$ in that node's notation and with the present scheme $H$ as its etale scheme. It yields a section over $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Restriction to $U_B$ and the isomorphism $H_{U_B}\cong P_B$ of step 15 give a section $s:U_B\to P_B$ of the actual pullback projection $\pi_n$.

source.place: Tags 04GH and 04GK (finite algebras and etale sections over strictly henselian rings); Morphisms Tag 01WN for the closed image.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-galois-cover-base-change] along the displayed map $U_n\to U$. Via its cartesian square, the given pullback $P_n=P\times_U U_n$ carries the pulled-back $G$-action and is a finite etale $G$-torsor. In particular every geometric fibre has simply transitive $G$-action. The finite morphism $\pi_n$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For each $g\in G$, the map $s_g=g\cdot s$ is a section: the action is over $U_n$, so $\pi_n\circ s_g=\pi_n\circ s=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper); base-change torsor statement as cited. Properness includes separatedness, Tag 01W1 (definition-proper).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion], each $s_g$ identifies $U_n$ with an open and closed subscheme $Q_g$ of $P_n$. These opens are pairwise disjoint and cover $P_n$. Indeed, over any geometric point $\bar u$ the torsor condition of [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois] says that $g\mapsto g\cdot s(\bar u)$ is bijective onto the geometric fibre. Thus every geometric point of $P_n$ lies in exactly one $Q_g$. A point in an intersection, or outside their union, would lift to a geometric point there, contradicting that bijectivity. Consequently the inverse maps $\pi_n|_{Q_g}:Q_g\to U_n$, followed by the $g$-indexed coprojection, glue on this disjoint open cover to a morphism $P_n\to\coprod_g U_n$. It is inverse to the morphism $\theta:\coprod_g U_n\to P_n$ whose $g$-component is $s_g$, since the two composites restrict to identities on each of these open pieces. The coproduct and its components are those of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family].

source.place: Tag 024T (proposition-properties-sections); the disjoint-cover inverse is written explicitly using the scheme gluing property of Tags 01JB/01JC.

proof.text: The isomorphism $\theta$ is equivariant for the left regular action on the index set $G$. For $h,g\in G$ its composite with $h$ on the target, restricted to the $g$-summand, is $h\cdot s_g=(hg)\cdot s=s_{hg}$, exactly the composite of the $g$-summand with the permutation $g\mapsto hg$ on the source followed by $\theta$. Equality on coproduct components gives equality of the morphisms. The inverse of $\theta$ is therefore the required equivariant trivialization. This argument uses the action law already part of the given torsor.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134; elementary action-law refinement from a scheme splitting to an equivariant torsor splitting.

proof.text: If $r=0$, the presentation has no variables or relations: $R_n=R$, and $f=1$, so $U_n=\operatorname{Spec}R=U$ with identity structure map for every positive $n$. Steps 2-19 therefore already trivialize $P\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Choosing $n=1$ gives the identical base scheme and the same equivariant trivialization, and $(1,p)=1$. The trivial group case also has $n=|G|=1$ and is included.

(7) field torsor components L_j of degree dividing n. (8) 032L applies with no excellence needed. (9) the total-quotient argument holds and 033C/034M make T integrally closed in D. (13) flatness over the PID A_i (0AUW), then 00RV/00RT and 00U6 (3)=>(2) give an etale neighbourhood. (14) W is open and contains U_B and every height-one point. (15) the codimension-two extension node applies to points of height at least 2, giving H. (16) H is surjective and a section exists over strictly henselian B.
